correctness.rationale: The exact domain is the group F_2^(2^4) with the indicator of all 168 antichain-incidence vectors. A 65-pair criterion exhaustively enumerates all 2^16 masks. Exact Walsh butterfly and independent direct sums over 168 antichains agree at all 65,536 frequencies; the signed spectrum has 6,611 zeros, hence rank 58,925. An independent direct zero-frequency summation verifies the Fourier-support kernel and its absolute sum 3,052,046, giving 1,526,023/32,768. The 48-action orbit census independently checks 199 zero orbits. Parseval and integer constraints hold. Translation averaging proves this is the minimum norm of any real or complex projection onto the range in l1 and linfinity, not just Fourier projections. All checker source files and exhaustive certificate tables are packaged.

originality.rationale: Distinct evaluated constants for the antichain-incidence ensemble were not present in the closest material inspected or bounded scientific database queries. Counting antichains (168) is classical and not claimed new, and general Fourier/translation-averaging principles are classical; the evaluated 6,611 nullity, 199 zero orbits, 79-level signed spectrum, and sharp 1,526,023/32,768 projection norm for this ensemble constitute the assessed claim. residual_risks: An unindexed antichain independence-polynomial computation or a pre-existing Fourier table could contain the same 168-point signed spectrum; bounded searches cannot rule out every source.
General signed independent-set partition functions include the object abstractly, but the evaluated exact constants were not identified in examined sources.
The evaluated finite invariants do not imply a general family formula for larger Boolean lattices or a lower bound beyond the stated endpoint norm.

value.rationale: All antichains of B4 are a canonical and much-studied Dedekind object, not a selected arbitrary slice. The rank 58,925 determines the exact dimension of recoverable signals from convolution by that family and the 6,611-dimensional nullspace; the optimal endpoint projection amplification 1,526,023/32,768 determines the best possible extraction stability without imposing translation invariance. These are distinct from the classical 168 enumeration. The 199 symmetry orbits give a compact natural classification of Fourier zeros. This exact finite result has intrinsic harmonic value although no asymptotic or higher-order theorem is asserted.
